title: Embedding serving observability checklist and trace plan
content:
Context:
This is a working checklist and trace/metrics plan for the embedding serving pipeline (embedding generation + retrieval hooks) to help product/infra teams instrument, detect regressions, and build compact dashboards with cost attribution. A lot of existing observability notes focus on text-generation flows; embeddings have different failure modes (batching stalls, memory spikes, vector dim mismatch, p99 tail from cold GPUs). This doc collects pragmatic signals, span naming, sampling heuristics, dashboard panel ideas, alerts, and quick investigation steps for SREs and oncall.

Objective:
- Define the minimal set of metrics to operate embedding endpoints at scale while keeping dashboard/query costs low.
- Provide trace span anchors and sampling rules to reconstruct high-latency or error flows.
- Propose a compact dashboard layout and alert thresholds that are actionable for owners.

Scope:
- Online embedding generation service (hosted API + dedicated pools).
- Does NOT include downstream vector DBs or client-side instrumentation (only server-side ingress and inference path).

Quick principles / constraints:
- Keep cardinality low: tag by tenant tier (free/prod/enterprise), model family, and batch-size-bucket (1, 2-8, 9-32, 33+). Avoid per-tenant panels unless high-cost tenant.
- Prioritize signals that map to action (eg: increased p99 inference time -> scale GPU pool / change quantization profile).
- Sample traces aggressively on errors and tail latency; low sampling for normal traffic.

Core metrics (definitions + units):
- embed.requests.count: total API requests (counter). Unit: requests. Tag: tenant_tier, model, batch_size_bucket.
- embed.batch_size.histogram: observed batch sizes (histogram). Unit: count. Useful for verifying batching config.
- embed.latency.infer.p50/p95/p99: model-only inference latency (ms). Important to separate model_infer and enqueue latencies.
- embed.latency.total.p50/p95/p99: end-to-end request latency (ms) including queueing + marshaling.
- embed.errors.count: number of failed embedding requests (counter) by error_kind (model_error, timeout, invalid_input).
- embed.kv_cache.hits / embed.kv_cache.misses: if prefix caching used for repeated prompt embeddings.
- embed.memory.gpu_utilization.percent: GPU memory usage by pool (percent).
- embed.cpu.scheduling.delay.ms: time spent waiting to schedule CPU work that prepares batches.
- embed.cost.per_request: derived metric = cost_model(token_ms, gpu_type, batch_size). Unit: USD (approx).

Metric tagging guidance:
- model: short id (e.g., text-embed-4-small)
- tenant_tier: free | standard | enterprise
- batch_size_bucket: 1 | 2-8 | 9-32 | 33+
- pool_region: us-west1 | eu-west1 | apac1

Span and trace naming (span anchors) - essential for trace-driven debugging:
- request.receive: starts at ingress/edge LB. Tags: request_id, tenant_id, route
- request.auth: auth/quotas check span
- batch.enqueue: time from per-tenant queue insertion to batch emission (use as indicator of batching stalls)
- batch.assemble: CPU work combining inputs into tensor batches
- model.infer: GPU work (this should be the heaviest span and include batch_size, model_name, seq_len)
- model.infer.kernels: optional inner spans if we instrument kernel selection/compilation
- kv_cache.lookup: optional, returns hit/miss metadata and item size
- response.serialize: marshalling and returning to client

Trace sampling rules:
- Full-trace (100%) for any request with embed.errors.count > 0 (error traces).
- Full-trace for requests with total latency > 2s (configurable threshold).
- 1% uniform sampling for normal traffic, with stratified over batch_size_bucket to ensure representation of large batches.
- 100% for synthetic probe runs and canary tenants.

Dashboard layout (compact 6-panel quick-runbook board):
Panel 1: Traffic & Batching overview- embed.requests.count (1m rate) by batch_size_bucket- embed.batch_size.histogram (sparkline)- Goal: detect sudden drop in batch sizes (indicates batching misconfiguration or plume of singletons)
Panel 2: Latency lanes (p50/p95/p99) end-to-end + model_infer overlay- One small panel per model-family with p99 prominently colored
Panel 3: Error surface and reasons- embed.errors.count by error_kind and by tenant_tier
Panel 4: Resource pressure- GPU mem% and GPU util% by pool_region; CPU scheduling delay heatmap
Panel 5: Cost attribution snapshot- embed.cost.per_request * requests by tenant_tier (top 10 tenants) - daily burn estimate
Panel 6: Trace anchors and recent long traces (links)

Alerting suggestions (actionable):
- P0: embed.errors.count increased > 3x baseline in 5m AND error_rate > 0.5% -> pager (possible model/pipeline break)
- P1: embed.latency.total.p99 > 1.5s for 10m -> slack alert to eng-observability and model-owner (possible GPU hot-spot)
- P2: GPU memory usage > 90% for 5m -> page SRE (scale or evict low-priority jobs)
- Cost guard: daily embed cost forecast > 150% of last 7 day rolling median -> oncall slack bot + finance-notify (investigate bursting tenants)

Runbook quick-steps for high p99 (short checklist):
1) Open the latency panel, identify affected model_family and batch_size_bucket.
2) Check batch.enqueue median/90th percentile to see if batching or queueing is the issue.
3) Inspect GPU pool metrics (utilization, memory) for hot nodes and recent deployments (match timestamps to deploy tags).
4) Pull last 20 traces sampled at >p99, look for model.infer kernel spikes or repeated kernel_compilation spans.
5) If errors present, check model health page (model-serving repo PR list) and revert canary if correlated.
6) If cost spike, identify top tenants by embed.cost.per_request * requests and throttle/notify as per policy.

Lightweight instrumentation snippets (examples to include in PRs):
- Add metric: emit embed.batch_size with tag batch_size_bucket at batch assembly point.
- Add span annotation: model.infer should include fields: model_name, batch_size, seq_len, gpu_type, kernel_variant.
- Emit embed.cost.per_request in post-processing with deterministic cost model tag (gpu_type, infer_ms).

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to attribute cost when multi-model fanout is used for hybrid embeddings? (proposal: split cost by model.infer.ms share)
- Should we add tenant-specific dashboards for top 20 spenders? (ops vs finance ask)
- Confirm retention for error traces: 90 days? (cost/infra tradeoff)
- Verify whether prefix caching for embeddings is used in any internal clients; add kv_cache metrics if so.

Short-term action items (owners & ETA):
- [Maya] Add embed.batch_size and embed.cost.per_request metrics to API handler (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/model-serving/pull/738) - ETA 2025-02-20
- [Jonas] Implement trace sampling rules in tracing-service config; 1% baseline + 100% errors - ETA 2025-02-26
- [Samira] Dashboard draft (6 panel board) + alert config - ETA 2025-02-28
- [Ravi] Cost model review with finance - ETA 2025-03-05

Notes to self / rough links:
- Slack thread: #embeddings-ops (see thread ts:16234012)
- Confluence: Observability embedding design doc draft (CONFLUENCE-ENG-EMB-102)

Appendix - useful query examples (prometheus / bigquery style pseudo-queries):
- requests per minute by batch bucket: rate(embed_requests_total[1m]) by (batch_size_bucket)
- model infer p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(embed_infer_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model))
- cost per tenant (daily): sum by (tenant_id) (rate(embed_requests_total[1d]) * embed_cost_per_request)

If you pick this up: copy to new doc for private-dedicated variants (pool-level dashboards) and mark changes to sampling percent for lower-volume dedicated pools.

End of working notes.
